root_cause.text: An off-by-one error in the liquidio PF `setup_nic_devices()` failure cleanup used `while (i--)`, which skipped freeing the current failed `ifidx` in the NIC device array and leaked the partially initialized device.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states “The current cleanup loop while(i--) skip the failing index i, causing a memory leak,” and the patch changes the cleanup from `while (i--)` to `do { ... liquidio_destroy_nic_device(octeon_dev, i); } while (i--);` while also adding `i--;` in the `devlink_alloc` failure path so cleanup starts from the last successfully allocated index.

intent_record.intent_summary: Decrement the initialized-device index on devlink allocation failure so cleanup only processes successfully created NIC devices.
intent_record.what: A decrement of the loop/index variable `i` was added in the `if (!devlink)` error path immediately before jumping to `setup_nic_dev_free`.
intent_record.how: When `devlink` allocation fails, the code now reduces the count/index of successfully initialized NIC devices before entering cleanup, preventing the cleanup path from treating the failed iteration as successfully created and potentially freeing or accessing an uninitialized entry.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix NIC setup failure cleanup so the current interface index is always destroyed and reported, including index 0.
intent_record.what: The cleanup loop in setup_nic_devices() was changed from a post-tested decrementing while loop `while (i--) { ... }` to a do-while loop `do { ... } while (i--);`, keeping the same loop body that logs the failed NIC index and destroys the NIC device.
intent_record.how: This makes the cleanup body execute at least once before checking `i--`, so the current NIC index `i` is also cleaned up when setup fails. Previously, if failure occurred with `i` at 0, the loop body would not run at all, and more generally the failing index itself could be skipped due to the post-decrement condition being evaluated before entering the loop.

relevance_review.reason: The change adjusts the device index on a failure path so cleanup iterates only over successfully created NIC devices, directly addressing the off-by-one cleanup bug that otherwise skips or mishandles the failed/current entry.

The change directly fixes the NIC setup failure cleanup off-by-one behavior by ensuring the current failed interface index, including index 0, is destroyed and reported, matching the described root cause of skipped cleanup and leaked partial device state.

candidates.rationale: This loop condition embodies the off-by-one bug: post-decrement causes cleanup to start from i-1, skipping the currently failed ifidx stored in i and leaking that partially initialized NIC device.
On devlink allocation failure this jumps into the buggy cleanup path without adjusting i, so the subsequent while (i--) cleanup skips freeing the current interface index.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop condition is the direct off-by-one root cause. Using post-decrement starts cleanup from i - 1, so the currently failed interface index stored in i is skipped, including the index 0 case, leaking the partially initialized NIC device.

This jump can enter the buggy cleanup path with i still referring to the current failed interface index. Because the cleanup loop uses the off-by-one condition, that current index is not freed, contributing to the leak on this failure path.

In the error label `setup_nic_dev_fail:`, cleanup is performed with `while (i--) { ... liquidio_destroy_nic_device(octeon_dev, i); }`. Because post-decrement is used as the loop condition, when initialization fails for the current interface index `i`, the first cleanup iteration runs with `i - 1`, not the current failed `i`. This matches the root cause: the partially initialized current `ifidx` is skipped and not freed. The function also stores the allocated device before later failure points via `props = &octeon_dev->props[i]; props->netdev = netdev;`, so a failure after allocation can leave `octeon_dev->props[i].netdev` set for the current `i`, yet the cleanup loop will not call `liquidio_destroy_nic_device()` on that index. No corrected cleanup that includes the current `i` (such as decrementing after freeing or explicitly handling `i`) is present, so the fix is not in this version.
